question: A 26-year-old nurse presents 12 hours after she accidentally stuck herself with a blood-contaminated needle. She reported the accident appropriately and now seeks post-exposure prophylaxis. She does not have any complaints at the moment of presentation. Her vital signs include: blood pressure 125/80 mm Hg, heart rate 71/min, respiratory rate 15/min, and temperature 36.5℃ (97.7℉). Physical examination is unremarkable. The nurse has prescribed a post-exposure prophylaxis regimen which includes tenofovir, emtricitabine, and raltegravir. How will tenofovir change the maximum reaction rate (Vm) and Michaelis constant (Km) of the viral reverse transcriptase?

options.opa: Vm will decrease, Km will stay the same
options.opb: Vm and Km will both decrease
options.opc: Vm will decrease, Km will increase
options.opd: Vm will stay the same, Km will increase
options.ope: Vm and Km will both increase

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Tenofovir is a nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor" -> "inhibits viral reverse transcriptase activity" -> "reduces the maximum reaction rate (Vm)" -> "Km remains unchanged due to competitive inhibition" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Tenofovir targets reverse transcriptase" -> "inhibits the enzyme's function" -> "leads to a decrease in Vm" -> "Km does not change as it is not a substrate" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Tenofovir acts on viral reverse transcriptase" -> "decreases the enzyme's maximum reaction rate (Vm)" -> "Km is not affected as it does not alter substrate affinity" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Tenofovir inhibits reverse transcriptase" -> "results in decreased Vm" -> "Km remains constant as it does not affect binding affinity" -> 88%
analysis: Tenofovir is a nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI) that competes with the natural substrate for the active site of the viral reverse transcriptase enzyme. As a competitive inhibitor, tenofovir will decrease the maximum reaction rate (Vm) because it reduces the overall rate of reaction when the substrate concentration is high. However, it does not change the Michaelis constant (Km) because Km is a measure of the affinity of the enzyme for the substrate, which remains unchanged in the presence of a competitive inhibitor. Therefore, Vm will decrease, and Km will stay the same.
